title: Ecosystem Stability and Biodiversity
seo_title: Biodiversity Worksheets: Succession, Invasive Species and Human Impacts (Biology)
standard_text: Evaluate claims, evidence, and reasoning that the complex interactions in ecosystems maintain relatively consistent numbers and types of organisms in stable conditions, but changing conditions may result in a new ecosystem. Design, evaluate, and refine a solution for reducing the impacts of human activities on the environment and biodiversity.
meta_desc: Free high school biology worksheets on ecosystem stability and biodiversity (NGSS HS-LS2-6, HS-LS2-7): succession, keystone and invasive species, survey data and solutions. 100 questions with answers.
key_sub: Big changes can create a new ecosystem; smart solutions reduce human impacts.
body_html:
How to think about it

Stable ecosystems stay similar; big changes can make new ones.

  • Many interacting species keep numbers fairly steady. More biodiversity → more stability.
  • After a disturbance: primary succession (no soil) or secondary succession (soil remains).
  • Human impacts (habitat loss, pollution, invasive species, overharvesting, climate change) need targeted solutions.
Example

A fire burns a forest but leaves soil. Which succession?

Soil remains

Answer: secondary

Example

Site A: 8 species, 40 animals. Site B: 2 species, 100 animals. More biodiverse?

Count species, not individuals

Answer: site A

Common mistakes

  • Thinking an ecosystem never changes.
  • Thinking more individuals means more biodiversity.
  • Thinking invasive species are harmless.

faq.q: What is the difference between primary and secondary succession?
faq.a: Primary succession starts on bare rock with no soil. Secondary succession starts after a disturbance that leaves soil behind.

faq.q: Why does biodiversity make ecosystems more stable?
faq.a: With many species, if one declines, others can fill its role, so the ecosystem recovers better.

faq.q: How can people reduce their impact?
faq.a: Protect habitats, build wildlife corridors, control invasive species, set catch limits and reduce pollution and emissions.

items.q: What is ecological succession?
c: a gradual change in the species in an area over time

items.q: Beavers build dams that create ponds. What is the most likely result?
c: Mussels take over and fewer species remain.
Many new wetland species can live there.
Urchins increase and kelp forests shrink.
items.e: A keystone species has a large effect.

items.q: What is an invasive species?
c: a non-native species that spreads and harms an ecosystem

items.q: What is a keystone species?
c: a species with a large effect on its ecosystem compared with its numbers
a species found only in caves

items.q: A disease kills most of the starfish on a rocky shore. What is the most likely result?
c: Elk browse less by rivers, and willows and beavers return.
Many new wetland species can live there.
Mussels take over and fewer species remain.
items.e: A keystone species has a large effect.

items.q: A forest fire burns trees but leaves the soil. Which kind of succession follows?
items.e: Primary starts with no soil; secondary starts where soil remains.

What is biodiversity?
c: the variety of living things in an area
the number of animals of one kind

items.q: What are pioneer species?
c: the first organisms to live in a bare area, like lichens and mosses

items.q: Why are diverse ecosystems more stable?
c: If one species declines, others can fill its role.
